correctness.rationale: The image of the group identity remains a right operand acting trivially. Using it in the medial law forces all right translations to commute; thus the commutators of conjugations, which act by G', are trivial in any medial image. Conversely, normality of G' gives a well-defined orbit quotient, because changing a right operand by G'-conjugacy preserves its coset, and the quotient translations commute. Self-distributivity then makes their labels unchanged by right translations, which gives mediality. For S_n, the derived group is A_n. The index-two orbit splits exactly when the centralizer has no odd element: an even cycle or a swap of equal odd cycles gives an odd centralizer element, and in the absence of both the centralizer is generated by even cycle powers. Thus the split types and parity action are exactly as stated. A split type exists for every n>=3 (n odd, or n-1 plus 1 when n is even), and an odd type exists. The two distinct translations determine parity intrinsically; a quandle automorphism commutes with the sole nonidentity translation and preserves parity, and these conditions suffice. The centralizer of the disjoint pair swaps and the independent permutations of each singleton type yield the stated group and central quotient.
residual_risks: Recorded finite tests are corroborative, not the proof for arbitrary n. The supplied script was inspected, not executed.
